  • Tuning preference changes and their durable ledger records are one governed operation: a ledger failure restores the exact prior preference, while rollback is idempotent and retry-safe. Historical duplicate rows imported from an older release remain historical evidence; new v0.1.2 observations converge on the normalized rule.
  • Approvals, scheduler health, and tuning evidence make the reason, recommended action, attempts, and latest success or error visible without turning a model suggestion into decision authority.
  • Auto-tuning now uses one attention-ordered rule-review workspace instead of duplicating recommendations in a separate queue. Its three-state evidence strip, responsive rows, and focused inspector distinguish collecting, within-policy, and needs-attention rules without presenting model verdicts as analyst learning.
  • Intelligence now exposes five direct, non-overlapping destinations—Knowledge corpus, Reference runbooks, Operator memory, Response playbooks, and Agent personas—without hiding Personas behind a second in-page tab switcher. The old #/catalog deep link remains a compatibility alias for Response playbooks.
  • Runbooks and Playbooks are durable operator catalogs layered over immutable bundled content. Runbooks remain retrieval guidance; Playbooks remain selected procedures; neither can override deterministic case policy.
  • The protected reference catalog adds cloud-IAM compromise and data-exfiltration guidance, plus exact-match cloud-identity, exfiltration, and ransomware procedures. Two specialist personas cover cloud identity and data protection without adding a second agent engine or turning keyword similarity into procedure selection.
  • Case Manager records the latest investigation's actual knowledge, approved memory, runbook, playbook, and tuning inputs. It does not infer use from enabled settings or leak earlier investigation inputs into a later run.
  • Telemetry-source recommendations require versioned query or tool evidence for a specific investigation gap. Until a connector-neutral controlled query boundary emits that proof, the Console reports capture unavailable; connector absence by itself never creates a recommendation.

docs.title: Operations, export, and release handling
docs.text:
• Authorized administrators can export supported application-state scopes through resumable, response-bounded segments rather than treating 5,000 records as a lifetime ceiling. Cursors stay actor, scope, and snapshot bound; secrets and raw source telemetry remain excluded.
  • The source-discovery and coherent-pair activation work established prerequisites for supervised updates, but 0.1.2 did not publish the supervisor, signed plan, or host bootstrap as an installable release. Those capabilities are included in the later 0.1.5 release candidate and become installable only if that candidate completes Stable publication; 0.1.3 also remained an unpublished snapshot.
  • Settings can separately observe public Stable and Testing source revisions. That read-only GitHub metadata is a review aid and can never deploy, activate, restart, migrate, or roll back the application.
  • The installed Help Center remained part of the Web artifact at /docs/0.1/. Because no v0.1.2 tag was published, it never became an immutable public release or updater source.
  • Repository contribution hygiene now includes a Code of Conduct, structured issue forms, support routing, a pull-request checklist, and generated release-note categories. Repository description and license remain explicit owner/legal decisions rather than guessed source changes.

docs.title: Console and analyst workflow
docs.text:
• Case Manager, Workspace Chat, setup, Settings, loading states, and the shared shell use the standardized Agentic SOC design system and retain Light, Dark, System, narrow-width, keyboard, and reduced-motion behavior.
  • The Console presents exact source/model execution provenance and recorded Standard, Flex, Batch, or Unconfirmed cost tiers without inferring a provider discount that the ledger did not record.
  • Noise reduction, case lifecycle, effectiveness, and tuning outcomes keep unavailable cohorts explicit rather than manufacturing saved time, causal improvement, or provider-invoice precision.

The historical change inventory is in the 0.1.2 changelog.

docs.title: Historical boundary
docs.text:
The 0.1.2 snapshot is not a supported upgrade source and has no release evidence or immutable identity to verify. Do not bootstrap from it, publish it, or create a replacement tag. Operators upgrading from the published v0.1.1 release must use the current upgrade procedure and the first later exact annotated release that passes its complete gate.

For the active publication checklist, build identity, supported updater topology, rollback limits, and exact command sequence, use the 0.1.5 release record, Known limitations, and Release channels and versioning.

docs.title: Agentic SOC 0.1.3
docs.text:
Agentic SOC 0.1.3 was a backward-compatible beta candidate in the 0.1 documentation line. Its accepted source reached Testing/main, but no immutable annotated v0.1.3 tag, GitHub Release, signed upgrade plan, or supported Stable image set was published. It remains here only as a historical Testing record.

Unpublished snapshot — do not deploy or tag

There is no official v0.1.3 release artifact or updater source. Do not create that tag retroactively, relabel a source build as Stable, or execute old tag and bootstrap commands copied from an earlier draft. The governed successor is Agentic SOC 0.1.5.

docs.title: Snapshot highlights
docs.text:
The 0.1.3 candidate added or hardened:

  • the isolated supervised-update implementation for the reference single-replica PostgreSQL Compose topology, including signed-plan verification, digest-pinned application images, verified backup, durable progress, and image rollback;
  • cloud-IAM compromise and data-exfiltration runbooks, exact-match response playbooks, and dedicated cloud-identity and data-protection personas;
  • truthful detection-rule authoring, evidence states, collaboration degradation, Standup degradation, responsive Rules and Case Manager layouts, and shared empty states; and
  • stricter release acceptance, immutable action and Docker-base references, fail-closed workflow policy, separate deployment/updater checks, real reference PostgreSQL readiness, and shipping-image builds.

These capabilities are included in the 0.1.5 release candidate together with the actual Stable publication artifacts. See the 0.1.5 release record and changelog for the complete promoted scope.

docs.title: Why this is not Stable
docs.text:
SemVer and channel provenance are separate. A package or source tree can report 0.1.3 while remaining Testing. Stable identity additionally requires:

  • the exact accepted main commit;
  • an immutable annotated tag with matching version;
  • successful fail-closed CI on Testing, main, and that tag;
  • public digest-pinned backend, Console, and updater images;
  • image signatures tied to the exact tagged release workflow identity;
  • a signed canonical upgrade plan and Sigstore bundle; and
  • an immutable GitHub Release containing the verified canonical asset inventory.

None of those publication artifacts exists for 0.1.3. The last Stable release before 0.1.5 is v0.1.1.

docs.title: Historical boundary
docs.text:
Version 0.1.3 must never be used as an operational bootstrap identity or newly published tag. A mutable/source-built 0.1.3 deployment must follow the current upgrade procedure to enter the canonical signed Stable line. If a post-publication correction is needed after v0.1.5, prepare a new patch; never repair history by creating or moving v0.1.3.

For current compatibility, rollback limits, exact artifacts, verification commands, and immutable-tag procedure, use Agentic SOC 0.1.5, Known limitations, and Release channels and versioning.

docs.title: Agentic SOC 0.1.4 failed publication
docs.text:
Agentic SOC 0.1.4 reached the accepted main source tree and received the immutable annotated tag v0.1.4 on 5 August 2026. Its complete application CI, exact-tag CI, documentation build, and GitHub Pages deployment passed. The signed release workflow then stopped before building any release artifact.

Not an installable Stable release

v0.1.4 has no published GitHub Release, GHCR release images, immutable image digests, image signatures, upgrade-plan.json, or Sigstore plan bundle. Do not bootstrap, install, or relabel a deployment from this tag. v0.1.1 remains the last verified installable Stable release until a corrected newer publication completes. The subsequent immutable v0.1.5 attempt also failed before its canonical plan and GitHub Release; the current corrected candidate is 0.1.6.

docs.title: What succeeded
docs.text:
• The accepted 0.1.4 source was promoted through the protected Testing-to-main path.
  • The exact v0.1.4 tag CI run passed every independent lane and the fail-closed CI passed aggregate.
  • The version-matched 0.1 Help Center built and its immutable-tag documentation deployment succeeded.
  • No updater trust, signing, image, migration, or deterministic-decision boundary was bypassed.

docs.title: What failed
docs.text:
The release publisher's draft-inventory step correctly classified the initial remote state as:

{
  "release_state": "absent",
  "release_exists": false,
  "plan_exists": false,
  "bundle_exists": false
}

The workflow extracted the valid boolean fields with jq -e. By definition, jq -e returns exit status 1 when its result is the JSON value false, so set -e stopped the job even though the classifier had reported the expected empty starting state. The failure occurred before QEMU/buildx setup, image publication, signing, plan generation, or GitHub Release creation. There is no partial release state to resume.

docs.title: Immutable disposition
docs.text:
The tag is historical evidence and must never be deleted, moved, force-updated, or reused. Because the repair changes release code referenced by the tag, the old workflow cannot be repaired by rerunning v0.1.4; release discipline requires a new patch version.

The current corrected candidate is Agentic SOC 0.1.6. It carries the exact accepted 0.1.4 application scope, fixes boolean extraction without weakening the classifier, and repeats the complete Testing, promotion, main, tag, signing, anonymous-pull, canonical-bootstrap, and browser gates.

docs.title: Operator action
docs.text:
• Do not use git switch --detach v0.1.4 as an update bootstrap.
  • Do not expect /releases/download/v0.1.4/upgrade-plan.json or a 0.1.4 GHCR image to exist.
  • Keep an existing canonical v0.1.1 deployment unchanged until v0.1.6 is fully published and independently verified.
  • Reconcile Testing/source-built 0.1.3 or 0.1.4 deployments manually; neither is an immutable signed Stable installation source.

See Release channels and versioning, Upgrades and promotion, and the 0.1.6 release record for the active procedure and the 0.1.5 failed-publication record for the intervening immutable history.

docs.title: Agentic SOC 0.1.5
docs.text:
Agentic SOC 0.1.5 is an immutable, non-installable publication attempt. Its source carried the accepted 0.1.4 application scope, repaired that attempt's release-inventory parser, and tightened shipping-image dependency checks. The v0.1.5 workflow built and signed candidate component digests, but stopped in its anonymous multi-platform pull gate before publishing the canonical signed plan, Sigstore plan bundle, GitHub Release, or Stable convenience tags.

Those partial registry objects are not installation authority. The corrected release is 0.1.6; v0.1.5 must never be moved, deleted, recreated, or reused.

Do not install, bootstrap, or update from v0.1.5

The annotated tag exists, but the complete release evidence does not. There is no canonical public GitHub Release containing upgrade-plan.json and upgrade-plan.sigstore.json, so the supervisor has no authenticated 0.1.5 plan to consume. Candidate tags and signed image digests created by the failed workflow are inert and must not be copied into an override manually.

docs.title: What the attempt contained
docs.text:
The source tree recorded by v0.1.5 included:

  • the accepted Security Command Center, Case Manager, Workspace Chat, runbook, playbook, Intelligence, approval, export, and installed Help Center scope;
  • OpenAI live Flex preference with truthful Standard fallback and one usage ledger;
  • a reviewed wheel version compatible with the backend runtime's constrained packaging dependency;
  • pip check inside both backend image build stages and the final image CI gate; and
  • a corrected release-inventory parser that treats valid JSON false values as data.

See the 0.1.2 historical snapshot, 0.1.3 historical snapshot, 0.1.4 failed publication record, and changelog for the accumulated application inventory.

docs.title: Exact failure boundary
docs.text:
The release workflow successfully:

  1. verified the immutable annotated tag and exact accepted main commit;
  2. required the exact successful tag CI aggregate;
  3. built public multi-architecture candidate images for backend, Console, and updater;
  4. resolved their immutable index digests; and
  5. signed and verified each digest with the exact tagged release-workflow identity.

Publication then stopped while proving anonymous Docker pulls. The gate pulled linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 through the same index-digest reference in one classic Docker image store. Docker retained the first selected platform under that reference and rejected the second, even though the remote index and both child manifests were valid and public.

Because the workflow stopped there, version 0.1.5 has none of the canonical installable release objects:

  • no public GitHub Release;
  • no canonical upgrade-plan.json;
  • no canonical upgrade-plan.sigstore.json;
  • no Stable backend:v0.1.5, webui:v0.1.5, or updater:v0.1.5 convenience tag;
  • no canonical bootstrap receipt; and
  • no enabled in-app update path.

The candidate image digests and their Sigstore attachments are forensic evidence of the failed run only. They cannot substitute for the absent signed plan and published Release.

docs.title: Why the tag cannot be repaired
docs.text:
The release job executes the workflow stored in the immutable tag commit. A later workflow correction cannot change that source by rerunning v0.1.5. Moving the tag would destroy its audit identity, while deleting and recreating it would violate the release contract.

The only valid recovery is a strictly newer patch release that repeats every gate. Version 0.1.6 preserves the tag, corrects the anonymous pull verifier, rebuilds and signs new component digests, generates and signs a new plan, publishes a new GitHub Release, and exercises the canonical supervised bootstrap independently.

docs.title: Operator action
docs.text:
Do not run bootstrap, artifact-download, image-pin, or tag-creation commands from this historical page. Use the 0.1.6 release procedure only after all evidence it requires is present, or continue using a previously verified Stable release.

For the general immutable promotion and recovery policy, read Release channels and versioning. For the supported supervisor boundary, read Upgrades and promotion and Known limitations.

docs.title: Agentic SOC 0.1.6
docs.text:
Agentic SOC 0.1.6 is the corrected governed Stable candidate after the immutable, non-installable v0.1.5 publication attempt. It republishes the exact accepted 0.1.5 application scope under a new version and repairs the final anonymous multi-platform registry acceptance boundary. It remains in the 0.1 documentation line.

Verify the immutable release before installation

A source checkout, branch head, version string, candidate image, or signed image alone is not a Stable release. Version 0.1.6 is installable only when the annotated tag v0.1.6 resolves to the accepted main commit, the exact-tag CI and release workflows succeed, the GitHub Release contains the canonical signed plan and bundle, and every digest in that plan is anonymously readable. If any evidence is absent, continue using a previously verified Stable release.

The immutable v0.1.5 tag is a failed publication record. Its workflow built and signed candidate component digests but stopped before publishing the signed plan, Sigstore plan bundle, GitHub Release, or Stable convenience tags. Those partial objects are not an installation source and the tag must never be moved.

docs.title: What changed after 0.1.5
docs.text:
The anonymous GHCR gate no longer pulls linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 through one local Docker reference. Docker can reuse or overwrite that local reference between platform pulls even when both remote manifests are valid. That false failure stopped the 0.1.5 release workflow after candidate images were built and signed.

For 0.1.6, the workflow still performs a real credential-free Docker pull for each required platform, but removes the exact digest reference after each pull so Docker's classic image store cannot retain one architecture under the shared index name. Its independent credential-free registry verifier remains the authoritative proof: it downloads and hashes the exact OCI index, requires exactly linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, downloads and hashes both child manifests and their configs, and verifies every required release label. A missing/private package, failed platform pull, unexpected platform, digest mismatch, or label mismatch still fails closed before the plan or GitHub Release can be published.

No application-state schema migration is introduced. The corrected release repeats the complete candidate, promotion, exact-tag, artifact, bootstrap, and browser acceptance sequence; no 0.1.5 result substitutes for a 0.1.6 gate.

docs.title: Carried Stable scope
docs.text:
The release carries the complete accepted product scope documented in the 0.1.5 failed publication record, including:

  • the Security Command Center and canonical split-pane Case Manager;
  • durable Workspace Chat and governed runbook/playbook catalogs;
  • explainable Intelligence inputs, analyst-confirmed tuning, approvals, export, and the version-matched installed Help Center;
  • OpenAI live Flex preference with truthful Standard fallback and one cost ledger;
  • signed, supervised updates for the supported PostgreSQL Compose topology; and
  • the hardened Console, accessibility, packaging, documentation, and fail-closed CI contracts accumulated through the 0.1 beta patches.

The model, memory, runbook, and playbook layers remain advisory. Deterministic code continues to own the final close/escalate route.

docs.title: Immutable release artifacts
docs.text:
The canonical repository is ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana. After successful publication, the workflow exposes these convenience tags:

ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/backend:v0.1.6
ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/webui:v0.1.6
ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/updater:v0.1.6

Convenience tags are not update authority. The signed plan contains only immutable digest references:

ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/backend@sha256:<digest>
ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/webui@sha256:<digest>
ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/updater@sha256:<digest>

The public GitHub Release must contain exactly:

upgrade-plan.json
upgrade-plan.sigstore.json

Canonical asset URLs are:

https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana/releases/download/v0.1.6/upgrade-plan.json
https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana/releases/download/v0.1.6/upgrade-plan.sigstore.json

The expected keyless Sigstore certificate identity and OIDC issuer are:

https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v0.1.6
https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com

The same workflow identity signs each image digest and the canonical release plan. The updater verifies that identity, issuer, repository, annotated tag, dereferenced tag commit, release version, compatibility envelope, and exact component digests.

docs.title: Signed plan contract
docs.text:
The plan is canonical JSON data, never a script or Compose fragment. The workflow publishes the following schema-v1 shape with concrete values:

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "product": "agentic-soc",
  "release": {
    "version": "0.1.6",
    "tag": "v0.1.6",
    "channel": "stable",
    "commit_sha": "<40-character lowercase tag commit SHA>",
    "published_at": "<timezone-qualified ISO-8601 timestamp>"
  },
  "compatibility": {
    "from": {"min_inclusive": "0.1.1", "max_exclusive": "0.2.0"},
    "state_backends": ["postgres"],
    "state_schema": 1,
    "compose_sha256": "e3f7ecbb0f749cc9d88f4392c58c9a63ddbd064e80ecde9f21fe9de199086fd4",
    "minimum_updater_protocol": 1,
    "backup_required": true,
    "migration": {"strategy": "none"}
  },
  "components": {
    "updater": {
      "image": "ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/updater@sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>",
      "digest": "sha256:<same updater digest>",
      "labels": {
        "org.opencontainers.image.version": "0.1.6",
        "org.opencontainers.image.revision": "<same tag commit SHA>",
        "org.opencontainers.image.source": "https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana",
        "dev.tlsoc.release.channel": "stable",
        "io.agentic-soc.state.schema": "1"
      }
    },
    "backend": {
      "image": "ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/backend@sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>",
      "digest": "sha256:<same backend digest>",
      "labels": {
        "org.opencontainers.image.version": "0.1.6",
        "org.opencontainers.image.revision": "<same tag commit SHA>",
        "org.opencontainers.image.source": "https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana",
        "dev.tlsoc.release.channel": "stable",
        "io.agentic-soc.state.schema": "1"
      }
    },
    "webui": {
      "image": "ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/webui@sha256:<64 lowercase hex characters>",
      "digest": "sha256:<same webui digest>",
      "labels": {
        "org.opencontainers.image.version": "0.1.6",
        "org.opencontainers.image.revision": "<same tag commit SHA>",
        "org.opencontainers.image.source": "https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana",
        "dev.tlsoc.release.channel": "stable",
        "io.agentic-soc.state.schema": "1"
      }
    }
  },
  "rollout": {
    "backend_timeout_seconds": 300,
    "webui_timeout_seconds": 180,
    "observation_seconds": 30
  }
}

After plan and image verification, the updater alone derives the release-specific Compose override:

# Generated by the Agentic SOC updater. Do not edit.
services:
  agentic-soc-updater:
    image: ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/updater@sha256:<verified updater digest>
  tlsoc-backend:
    image: ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/backend@sha256:<verified backend digest>
  tlsoc-webui:
    image: ghcr.io/arydestroyer/agentic-kibana/webui@sha256:<verified webui digest>

The plan cannot supply service names, host commands, paths, credentials, infrastructure images, arbitrary URLs, or Compose text. The generated override cannot mutate the frozen base.

docs.title: Compatibility and migration
docs.text:
The supervised path supports only the canonical, single-replica standalone Compose deployment with PostgreSQL-owned application state, canonical service/container/ network names, the canonical PostgreSQL volume, durable secrets, TLSOC_AUTH_ENABLED=true, and updater protocol 1.

The frozen deploy/docker-compose.agnostic.yml SHA-256 remains:

e3f7ecbb0f749cc9d88f4392c58c9a63ddbd064e80ecde9f21fe9de199086fd4

Release-specific version and digest pins exist only in the signed generated override. Changing that base requires a new protocol and manual bootstrap; it must never be hidden inside a patch plan.

SQLite, Elasticsearch-owned state, external PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, the legacy ELK merge, horizontal replicas, modified Compose topology, missing durable secrets, or unsupported migrations remain Manual upgrade required. PostgreSQL and Redis infrastructure remain operator-managed.

There is no application-state schema migration in 0.1.6. A catalog-verified PostgreSQL dump is still mandatory before application switching. Automatic rollback restores prior application image pins; database restore remains an explicit break-glass operation because restoring automatically could discard valid writes.

docs.title: Bootstrap and upgrade boundary
docs.text:
For a canonical deployment currently running supported Stable v0.1.1, use a clean checkout of the strictly newer, fully published v0.1.6 tag as the host-authorized bootstrap transport:

git fetch --tags origin
git switch --detach v0.1.6
test "$(git cat-file -t v0.1.6)" = tag
test "$(git rev-parse 'v0.1.6^{commit}')" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"

# .env must contain durable TLSOC_PG_PASSWORD, TLSOC_AUTH_ENABLED=true,
# TLSOC_AUTH_JWT_SECRET with at least 32 characters, and:
# AGENTIC_SOC_UPDATE_REPOSITORY=ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana
./scripts/bootstrap-updater.sh

The bootstrap verifies the exact release before installing or reconciling the private supervisor and applying its strictly newer plan. After the successful transition, use ./scripts/agentic-soc-compose.sh for every manual lifecycle operation so the active digest override and lifecycle lock remain in effect.

Source-built/Testing deployments and the non-installable 0.1.4 or 0.1.5 attempts cannot be relabelled Stable. Reconcile them manually to the canonical signed 0.1.6 deployment. A deployment already running 0.1.6 cannot bootstrap from the same plan; the updater deliberately requires a strictly newer target.

Read Upgrades and promotion and Known limitations before rehearsing the transition.

docs.title: Independent artifact verification
docs.text:
Verify that the remote exposes both the annotated tag object and its dereferenced commit before inspecting release assets:

git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana.git \
  refs/tags/v0.1.6 'refs/tags/v0.1.6^{}'

The command must return two different 40-character object IDs: the annotated tag object and the accepted main commit to which it dereferences.

Install a reviewed cosign version and verify the release plan:

tag=v0.1.6
repo=ARYDESTROYER/Agentic-Kibana
identity="https://github.com/${repo}/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/${tag}"
base="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"

curl --fail --location --output upgrade-plan.json "${base}/upgrade-plan.json"
curl --fail --location --output upgrade-plan.sigstore.json \
  "${base}/upgrade-plan.sigstore.json"

cosign verify-blob \
  --bundle upgrade-plan.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity "${identity}" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  upgrade-plan.json

Verify all three authenticated digest references with a fresh Docker configuration so cached credentials cannot satisfy the public-access test:

anonymous_docker_config="$(mktemp -d)"
for component in backend webui updater; do
  image="$(jq -er --arg component "${component}" \
    '.components[$component].image' upgrade-plan.json)"
  cosign verify \
    --certificate-identity "${identity}" \
    --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
    "${image}"
  DOCKER_CONFIG="${anonymous_docker_config}" docker buildx imagetools inspect \
    "${image}" >/dev/null
done

The release workflow additionally performs credential-free HTTP reads of each exact index, child manifest, and config. Repository administrators must make the three GHCR packages Public if anonymous reads return 401; package visibility is a GitHub setting and cannot be established by image push alone.

docs.title: Release acceptance
docs.text:
Publication requires the fail-closed CI passed aggregate on the frozen 0.1.6 candidate on Testing, the resulting content-equivalent main commit, and the exact immutable v0.1.6 tag. The release workflow then requires:

  1. the annotated tag and its dereferenced commit equal the accepted main SHA;
  2. all three dual-platform images build, carry exact Stable labels, and are signed;
  3. every image digest is anonymously readable and content-verified;
  4. the canonical plan passes schema, compatibility, digest, and Sigstore checks;
  5. the private draft contains exactly the canonical notes, plan, and bundle; and
  6. downloaded release assets byte-match before the draft becomes public.

The candidate must also pass the Console browser matrix and canonical PostgreSQL Compose bootstrap/update rehearsal. Never move, reuse, or repair a published tag. Any later defect receives a newer SemVer.

docs.title: Exact Stable build identity
docs.text:
Resolve every Stable stamp from the exact annotated tag on the accepted main commit. Never substitute a branch head, local clock, or unknown value:

git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git fetch --tags origin

release_version="$(tr -d '[:space:]' < VERSION)"
test "${release_version}" = "0.1.6"
release_sha="$(git rev-parse "v${release_version}^{commit}")"
test "${release_sha}" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
release_date="$(git show -s --format=%cI "${release_sha}")"

export TLSOC_VERSION="${release_version}"
export TLSOC_RELEASE_CHANNEL=stable
export TLSOC_BUILD_SHA="${release_sha}"
export TLSOC_BUILD_DATE="${release_date}"

Backend, Console, updater, /release.json, OCI labels, signed plan, tag, and GitHub Release must all resolve to the same version and commit. A mismatch fails safe to Testing and cannot authorize installation.

docs.title: Immutable annotated-tag checklist
docs.text:
Create the tag only after the clean candidate passes on Testing, promotion passes on the resulting main commit, and the final tree is frozen:

test "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < VERSION)" = "0.1.6"
test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
git tag -a v0.1.6 \
  -m "Agentic SOC 0.1.6" \
  -m "Corrected Stable beta publication: signed supervised updates, governed Intelligence, truthful operator states, and repaired anonymous multi-platform registry acceptance. Detailed notes: docs/releases/0.1.6.md; CHANGELOG.md."
test "$(git cat-file -t v0.1.6)" = tag
test "$(git rev-parse 'v0.1.6^{commit}')" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
git show --no-patch --show-signature v0.1.6
git push origin v0.1.6

Do not create the tag before all candidate/main gates pass, and never force, delete, move, or reassign it after push. See Release channels and versioning for the canonical promotion sequence.

docs.title: Agentic SOC 0.1
docs.text:
Agentic SOC 0.1 is the first standardized application and documentation release line. Human-facing documentation uses 0.1; the current source version is Semantic Version 0.1.6. It carries the accepted 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 Testing snapshots plus the exact accepted 0.1.4 and 0.1.5 application scope.

Builds on Testing are integration and acceptance builds. Version 0.1.6 is a supported Stable patch only when the accepted tree is on main, the resulting commit has passed the release gate, and that exact commit is tagged v0.1.6 with verifiable signed release artifacts and public image digests. If that evidence is incomplete, use a previously verified Stable release. The immutable v0.1.4 tag records a failed publication that produced documentation but no application artifacts. The immutable v0.1.5 workflow built and signed candidate image digests but stopped before the canonical plan, bundle, GitHub Release, and Stable tags. Neither is an update or bootstrap source. Branch state alone never establishes the installed release identity.

The repository uses Testing for integration and default main for accepted source. Patch 0.1.6 rebuilds the public and installed 0.1 guide without changing the documentation selector line; already-built artifacts keep their immutable bundled Help Center. Versions 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 remain unpublished historical Testing records. Versions 0.1.4 and 0.1.5 remain immutable failed-publication records, not installable Stable releases or artifact sources.

docs.title: What 0.1 provides
docs.text:
• Vendor-neutral pull and push ingestion normalized to OCSF.
  • Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and Wazuh pull connectors plus a broad receiver catalog.
  • Durable cursors, deterministic correlation/risk scoring, and source-scoped case identity.
  • Tiered model investigation through one cost-ledger gateway.
  • Deterministic close/escalate policy that the model, a playbook, or notification cannot override.
  • A Security Command Center with selected-window lifecycle KPIs, active risk, open/resolved composition, latest-case hover details, noise reduction, response timing, and deeper analytics. It defaults to visibility-aware five-second LIVE refresh and can expand Noise Reduction without exposing raw alert IDs.
  • Cases, traces, rationale, collaboration, feedback, campaigns, baselines, tuning, rules, and custom dashboards. Case Manager provides a persisted, accessible resizable split-pane active/all queue, a six-tab canonical detail workspace, redacted alert → cluster → case explanation, and permission-gated bulk operations. The Cases table remains available during migration and hands exact record links into Case Manager.
  • A personal Workspace Chat with newest-first searchable saved conversations, desktop history rail/narrow History Sheet, per-thread browser drafts, strict source selection, effective source/model provenance, bounded retention, and one docked composer. Case Manager Chat uses the same read-only engine while remaining case-scoped and outside personal Workspace history.
  • A standardized command-center Console grammar with a minimal identity-first sign-in, searchable flat Settings frame, persisted System/Light/Dark appearance, route-aware loading feedback, a bottom Documentation destination, and the targeted Entity investigation workflow. The sign-in surface keeps optional demo/SSO paths practical, removes marketing and synthetic audit copy, and honors narrow/reduced-motion states. Documentation opens the version-matched Help Center bundled with the app; GitHub is a secondary source/edit destination. The redundant Automated Scans screen remains deep-link compatible but is removed from primary navigation.
  • A browse/open/create/edit Playbooks manager for operator-authored Markdown; bundled procedures remain protected and every mutation is permission-gated, atomically reloaded, and audited.
  • A dedicated Intelligence → Runbooks workspace for protected bundled and durable operator-authored investigation guidance. Authorized operators can create, edit, delete, and reindex compact trusted references through optimistic revisions. New revisions enforce a 1,800-character, fixed-section plain-text body, a 1,200-character aggregate retrieval-metadata budget, and actionable Problem / Why / Fix validation; retrieval status and partial failures remain explicit, and deterministic case policy is unchanged.
  • PostgreSQL/pgvector, Elasticsearch, or SQLite application-state backends.
  • Local authentication, sessions, RBAC/custom roles, TOTP MFA, and OIDC SSO.
  • Provider-aware notifications, knowledge retrieval, enrichment, and spend controls.
  • Compatible official OpenAI alert/case calls prefer live Flex with truthful standard fallback by default; the independent asynchronous Batch queue remains opt-in.
  • An isolated five-source Demo Mode (Splunk, QRadar, Wazuh, syslog, and Microsoft Entra ID / Active Directory) and a bounded, audited, secret-free portable application-state export for authorized administrators.
  • A standalone React web console and version-matched Help Center served from the same application origin, with a complementary versioned public Stable site.

docs.title: Safe defaults and explicit choices
docs.text:
The balanced autopilot profile performs broad deterministic ingest/routing and enables a $10/day blocking LLM budget backstop. A blocked provider call routes work to human review rather than silently discarding it. NEEDS_HUMAN never auto-closes, and true-positive auto-close remains an explicit opt-in.

Authentication is off in the base configuration for isolated evaluation compatibility. Operators must enable authentication, replace demonstration credentials, configure HTTPS/secure cookies, and apply least privilege before shared use.

docs.title: Recommended deployment
docs.text:
Use the standalone Compose stack with PostgreSQL/pgvector for application state and Redis for caching. Connect source systems through scoped connector credentials. Existing Elasticsearch environments may instead hold Agentic SOC state in dedicated indices, using separate management and read-only log credentials.

Record the exact tag, image digests, commit SHA, build date, state backend, and /api/health/build-info response. A branch name alone is not a release identity. The Console badge shows v0.1.6 · Testing|Stable and exposes both Console and backend stamps; any identity mismatch is visibly downgraded to Testing.

docs.title: Important limitations
docs.text:
Version 0.1 does not claim:

  • high availability or horizontally coordinated workers;
  • a complete database migration/rollback framework;
  • an integrated durable secret manager;
  • durable pre-ack receipt semantics for every push transport;
  • multi-tenant row-level isolation by default;
  • production certification for every source/vendor combination;
  • that Agentic SOC ledger estimates equal provider invoices;
  • autonomous write-side response actions.

Use synthetic or non-sensitive data until the selected deployment, source protocol, model provider, backup, and failure behavior have been validated. Read the full Known limitations.

docs.title: Upgrade and support boundary
docs.text:
Back up the state store and deployment secrets before changing versions. Because 0.1 lacks a complete schema-migration framework, do not assume that starting an older image is a safe rollback; restore the matching pre-upgrade state when compatibility is not explicitly documented.

Start with Deployment, Security hardening, and Documentation versions. Read the detailed 0.1.6 Stable patch record before promoting or upgrading. The 0.1.5 failed-publication record and 0.1.4 failed-publication record are immutable but non-installable; the 0.1.3 record and 0.1.2 record remain historical unpublished Testing snapshots.

docs.title: Release channels and versioning
docs.text:
Agentic SOC's release contract has two channels and two long-lived branches. Work integrates on Testing. The accepted source tree is then promoted through a protected pull request to Stable on main, and the resulting main commit is verified. There is no third prerelease branch and no separate release-branch vocabulary.

Current repository topology

The remote now exposes both canonical branches and uses main as the default. Repository administrators must still keep the required pull-request gates and the CI passed aggregate enforced; a branch name alone never proves that a particular build passed acceptance.

docs.title: Channel contract
docs.text:
Channel Branch Intended use Publication Testing Testing Integrated changes, acceptance testing, upgrade rehearsal, and documentation review CI artifacts and documentation preview only Stable main Supported releases and deployment artifacts Immutable vX.Y.Z tag, versioned docs, and Stable image/package metadata 
flowchart LR
  F["Feature branch"] -->|pull request| T["Testing"]
  T --> G["Full release gate"]
  G -->|promotion PR; same source tree| M["main / Stable"]
  M --> V["vX.Y.Z tag"]
  V --> D["Versioned documentation"]

The branch names and channel names are deliberately different kinds of label:

  • write Testing when referring to the integration branch or channel;
  • write main when referring to the Git branch;
  • write Stable when referring to the release channel represented by main.

Do not use “alpha”, “Bleeding Edge”, “next”, or a generic “production branch” as synonyms for these channels.

For operators, this distinction is concrete: after main is provisioned, an ordinary clone or pull of main receives the last accepted Stable source tree, never in-progress work from Testing. Pulling Testing receives the current integration candidate and may include changes that have not passed release acceptance.

The Console's Settings → Organization → Updates & releases section observes these two source refs by default. A fork or renamed repository can replace the public GitHub URL and either branch name without changing the application wire namespace. This is metadata discovery only: an observed branch-head commit is linked for review and cannot deploy or activate itself. Stable discovery separately dereferences the exact annotated vVERSION tag; only that immutable tag commit can become an update candidate. For a bootstrapped supported deployment, the actual top-bar action additionally requires a newer Stable version, a compatible signed release plan, the private updater's preflight, durable secrets and PostgreSQL state, exact image digests, a verified backup, and recent built-in-super-admin reauthentication. After a successful installation, the same-origin Console manifest must still exactly match a healthy backend build before the new document activates.

docs.title: Version 0.1 nomenclature
docs.text:
The first standardized release line is documentation version 0.1. The current source version is product version 0.1.6. It carries the accepted 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 Testing snapshots plus the exact 0.1.4 and 0.1.5 application scope. The immutable v0.1.4 publication attempt produced documentation but no application artifacts. The immutable v0.1.5 workflow built and signed candidate image digests but stopped before publishing the canonical signed plan, GitHub Release, or Stable tags. Both are historical and non-installable. Version 0.1.6 is Stable only when the accepted main commit is immutably tagged v0.1.6 and its signed plan, public GitHub Release, and public digest-pinned images verify. If that evidence is incomplete, use a previously verified Stable release.

Surface Canonical value Product Agentic SOC Operator interface Agentic SOC Console Backend service/API Agentic SOC API SemVer package and image version 0.1.6 Git release tag v0.1.6 only from the exact verified main commit; absent before publication and immutable afterward Documentation selector and URL line 0.1 and /0.1/ Integration branch/channel Testing Stable branch/channel main / Stable

Patch releases remain within the same documentation line. For example, app versions 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.3, 0.1.4, 0.1.5, and 0.1.6 use the 0.1 documentation rather than creating new selector entries. A new minor release creates a new documentation line such as 0.2.

docs.title: Promotion procedure
docs.text:
Every release starts with a candidate commit on Testing:

  1. Merge focused feature branches into Testing through reviewed pull requests.
  2. Run the backend, web console, documentation, generated-contract, security, and deployment-configuration gates on that commit.
  3. Freeze the candidate while acceptance and upgrade checks run. Fix failures on a feature branch and merge them back into Testing; do not patch main first.
  4. Promote the accepted Testing source tree to main through a protected pull request. The merge commit may have a different SHA, but the promotion must not introduce content changes; re-run the complete gate on that resulting main SHA.
  5. Create the immutable vX.Y.Z tag from the verified main commit and publish artifacts from that SHA using the same X.Y.Z value from the root VERSION file.
  6. Let the documentation workflow publish the matching major.minor line and move the stable and latest aliases to it.

The Documentation workflow validates Testing and main, but publication is gated on the exact annotated vX.Y.Z tag. Its tag must match VERSION and resolve to the current origin/main commit. Configure the github-pages environment to admit the v* release-tag pattern, and keep Settings → Pages → Source set to GitHub Actions. A main push alone must never move the public Stable aliases.

Use an annotated tag and verify it before pushing:

git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
test "$(cat VERSION)" = "X.Y.Z"
test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
git tag -a "vX.Y.Z" \
  -m "Agentic SOC X.Y.Z" \
  -m "<operator-relevant release summary>. Detailed notes: docs/releases/X.Y.Z.md; CHANGELOG.md."
test "$(git cat-file -t 'vX.Y.Z')" = "tag"
test "$(git rev-parse 'vX.Y.Z^{commit}')" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
git show --no-patch "vX.Y.Z"
git push origin "vX.Y.Z"

Replace X.Y.Z with the real VERSION value and replace the summary placeholder with the release's concrete operator-visible scope. Publish the GitHub Release from that existing tag with the versioned release page and changelog as canonical notes. .github/release.yml defines repository PR-note categories but does not replace the canonical versioned release body. Published tags are immutable; never force-update one. The workflow first creates a non-public draft bound to the exact tag and commit SHA, uploads both canonical upgrade-plan assets, downloads and byte-compares them, verifies the Sigstore bundle, and only then changes the draft to published in one API transition. An interrupted retry may resume only that exact draft: an authenticated plan is reused, incomplete starter uploads are removed, and a missing signature bundle is recreated and verified before publication. A published release is never repaired or overwritten; a missing, duplicate, unexpected, or partial asset inventory fails closed and requires a new patch release. A later workflow retry may reuse the latest completed, successful ci.yml push run only when its tag ref and commit SHA exactly match that immutable release; it is deliberately not coupled to the retry's wall-clock time.

docs.title: Changelog discipline
docs.text:
CHANGELOG.md has exactly one active top-level [Unreleased] section during normal development. Dated work that is not a published release is a Development snapshot, not another [Unreleased] section and not a bracketed SemVer release.

As part of the final frozen release-preparation change:

  1. move the accepted entries out of [Unreleased] under [X.Y.Z] with the release date;
  2. open a new, empty [Unreleased] section above it;
  3. promote and verify that exact prepared tree on main; and
  4. tag that exact verified commit immediately.

If promotion is abandoned, revert the prepared release heading rather than leaving a Testing snapshot that reads as though it were published. Never keep multiple top-level [Unreleased] sections as a dated work log; the development journal and Development snapshot headings hold that history.

If a Stable defect is found, fix it through Testing, exercise the same gate, and promote a patch release. Emergency timing may shorten review windows, but it does not reverse the direction of promotion.

docs.title: Release gate
docs.text:
A candidate is promotable only when all required checks pass and the release notes describe its real operating boundary. At minimum:

  • canonical version metadata, OpenAPI, TypeScript contracts, image defaults, and release notes agree;
  • backend tests, web console lint/tests/build, and strict documentation build pass;
  • the supported PostgreSQL+pgvector/Redis state lane performs a real readiness write/read, and every shipping backend, Console, and updater image builds with the exact candidate identity before any tag can publish it;
  • workflow/ShellCheck and deploy/updater contracts run as separate required lanes so one early failure cannot hide another; the fail-closed CI passed aggregate must succeed on Testing, the resulting main commit, and the immutable tag;
  • the documented Console release-candidate browser matrix passes on the exact built candidate in Light, Dark, and System at desktop and narrow widths, with build SHA, release badge, keyboard/focus, loading/error/empty behavior, same-origin Help Center, and unexplained console/network errors recorded in a dated receipt;
  • deployment configuration validates and upgrade/restore steps are rehearsed for the affected state backend;
  • source credentials remain least-privilege and upstream systems remain read-only;
  • model errors fail safe to NEEDS_HUMAN, every model call remains cost-ledgered, and deterministic policy remains the sole close/escalate authority;
  • known limitations and migration steps are updated before promotion.

Passing unit tests does not by itself make a commit Stable. The accepted source, release metadata, documentation, and published artifacts must describe the same thing.

Never remove, soften, skip, or mark a required lane continue-on-error merely to make a release green. Repair the underlying contract and re-run the exact candidate. The application release and Stable Help Center publication both verify the exact tag CI run and its successful CI passed aggregate before publishing anything.

Use the release-candidate browser acceptance matrix for the required route and interaction coverage. A screenshot of one successful page is not a Console acceptance receipt.

docs.title: Build and badge provenance
docs.text:
SemVer and channel are independent. The 0.1.6 Testing candidate and its accepted Stable build can both report version 0.1.6; the channel says where that build sits in the acceptance lifecycle. Stamp the mutable provenance fields explicitly; keep or override the Dockerfile's canonical source URL as appropriate:

Variable Purpose TLSOC_VERSION Product/image SemVer; must match the root VERSION file TLSOC_RELEASE_CHANNEL testing for candidates; stable only for the verified main/tag build TLSOC_BUILD_SHA Exact source commit TLSOC_BUILD_DATE Reproducible build timestamp TLSOC_SOURCE_URL Dockerfile build argument for the canonical source repository URL stored in OCI metadata; the reference Compose files use its repository default

The authoritative backend value is /api/health/build-info.release_channel; images also carry dev.tlsoc.release.channel. The Console always shows a top-right vX.Y.Z · Testing|Stable badge. Opening it displays the Console and backend version, channel, commit, and build time separately. When both identities are available, only explicit matching Stable stamps render Stable; a version, channel, or known-SHA mismatch immediately downgrades the session badge to Testing. When backend build-info is unavailable, the immutable Console build stamp determines the visible channel and remains inspectable.

The web artifact also publishes a same-origin /release.json with its immutable version, channel, commit, and build time. Serve that file with no-store semantics. For a bootstrapped supported Compose/PostgreSQL deployment, the top bar may show Update vX.Y.Z when the backend observes a newer Stable release and the isolated updater reports a compatible protocol. Branch HEAD remains observation-only; the release candidate is bound to the dereferenced annotated tag commit. A freshly authenticated built-in super administrator must confirm a server-bound preflight. The updater then verifies the signed plan and digest-pinned artifacts, backs up owned state, performs the rollout, observes health, and automatically rolls back on failure. A completed rollout uses the existing no-store manifest, backend identity/readiness, and /index.html checks to reload the open tab; known unsaved drafts block that reload.

Separately, authenticated settings:read users may receive a read-only upstream observation from GET /api/releases/upstream. The backend checks only the saved public GitHub repository and Stable/Testing refs, caches successful metadata, and preserves a clearly marked last-known-good result when a later check fails. A higher SemVer or a same-version different SHA may be announced as source for review; an older SemVer is never called an update. POST /api/releases/upstream/check refreshes that metadata subject to a cooldown. Neither endpoint has Git, deployment, process, migration, or activation authority.

Neither source-observation endpoint is a release-promotion signal or deployment authority. Only the private updater socket can reach the host runtime, and its fixed v1 contract rejects browser-supplied URLs, commands, paths, Compose fragments, untrusted registries, infrastructure upgrades, and migrations. Deployments without that supervisor—or outside its exact reference profile—continue to use the manual upgrade path and receive a precise blocker instead of a misleading install button.

Local run-demo.sh derives Stable only from a literal main checkout; every other branch, detached checkout, or unknown channel fails safe to Testing unless an explicit release-build override is supplied. The documentation marquee is a separate publication badge controlled by TLSOC_DOCS_CHANNEL: the Testing docs job leaves it as Testing, while the main publication job explicitly sets Stable. No badge becomes Stable from SemVer or a similar-looking branch name alone.

CI follows the same rule: Testing pushes and pull requests are stamped Testing; the protected main build and canonical vX.Y.Z tag build are stamped Stable. Dockerfiles default to Testing, so an operator-built Stable image must supply the explicit channel, SHA, and build date rather than relying on a default.

docs.title: Semantic versioning before 1.0
docs.text:
Agentic SOC uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH SemVer for code, packages, and images:

  • increment PATCH for backward-compatible fixes within a documentation line;
  • increment MINOR for a new pre-1.0 capability set or a compatibility change that needs its own documentation line;
  • reserve MAJOR for the post-1.0 compatibility contract.

Before 1.0.0, a minor increment can contain breaking changes. Those changes must still have explicit migration notes and cannot be hidden behind the Testing/Stable channel labels.

docs.title: Version every published change, not every internal commit
docs.text:
Every published change to user-visible behavior, dependencies, configuration, public API contracts, documentation, packaging, or operational procedure receives a new SemVer and patch notes. Backward-compatible corrections in the existing 0.1 documentation line advance PATCH by one. The patch component is an integer, so 0.1.21 means patch 21; it is not a fourth-level version for a very small change.

A candidate may bundle several related commits and changes under one version. Internal refactors, test additions, review fixes, and intermediate commits do not each need their own version while they remain unpublished inside the same candidate. If the candidate has already been published and any release content changes—even only Stable documentation or an operational instruction—prepare the next patch instead of moving the existing tag or silently republishing its artifacts.

Each release record must cover the operator-visible change, compatibility and migration impact, rollback considerations, verification evidence, and known limitations. Choose the candidate version before final acceptance, align every artifact to it, promote the accepted tree to main, verify that exact main commit, and only then create its immutable Stable tag.

docs.title: Documentation publication
docs.text:
Every Console build first generates its own version-matched Help Center under /docs/<major.minor>/. That installed copy is part of the application artifact and is authoritative for operating that exact build. Public publication follows the same promotion direction as the source:

  • a pull request or push to Testing runs a strict docs-plus-app build and can publish a Development review artifact, but does not move the public Stable site;
  • the promoted main commit is a final verification input, not publication authority; only its matching immutable annotated release tag updates the current major.minor history with Mike, assigns the stable and latest aliases, and keeps older documentation directories;
  • the generated gh-pages branch is the version-history backing store; GitHub Pages itself must use GitHub Actions as its source, and the workflow deploys a validated link-free artifact with the native Pages actions;
  • the site version selector prefers the equivalent page in the selected version and falls back to that version's home page when the page did not yet exist.

The application rail opens the installed same-origin guide by default. GitHub and the public Stable/Development sites remain explicit secondary links for source editing, upgrade comparison, or future-work preview; they never replace installed help silently.

See Documentation versions for URL, alias, and maintenance rules, and Agentic SOC 0.1 for this release line.

docs.title: Documentation versions
docs.text: Agentic SOC ships version-matched documentation with the application. The documentation served by the running app is the authority for its controls and behavior; the public Stable site and Development source are secondary destinations for upgrade planning and previewing future work.

docs.title: Which documentation should I use?
docs.text:
Destination What it represents Use it for Installed version The Help Center built from the same accepted source as the running application and served on that application origin at /docs/0.1/ Daily use, administration, troubleshooting, and every decision about the running build Latest Stable Documentation built from the latest immutable release tag on the verified main source for the supported release line Upgrade evaluation, current supported guidance, and comparison with an older installation Development Documentation source integrated on Testing but not yet promoted and tagged Preview and review only; never assume it describes the installed application

Open Documentation from the bottom of the application navigation to enter the installed Help Center. GitHub remains the source/edit location and an escape hatch for newer material; it is not the primary product-help destination.

docs.title: Installed documentation contract
docs.text:
Every application build carries two related identifiers:

  • the full product SemVer, such as 0.1.6; and
  • the compatible documentation line, such as 0.1.

The documentation build and the application build originate from the same source commit. The web image includes the generated static Help Center and serves it from the same origin as the Console. That provides four useful guarantees:

  1. documentation remains available in an offline or isolated self-hosted deployment;
  2. following an in-app documentation link does not leave the application by default;
  3. the installed guide cannot silently change underneath a pinned application image;
  4. a release artifact and its instructions can be traced to the same source identity.

The installed Help Center does not show a blanket “may be outdated” warning. It is intentionally accurate for that installed build. A notice is appropriate only when the reader chooses an older public documentation version or follows a link to newer Stable or Development material.

docs.title: Version mapping
docs.text:
Documentation label Application SemVer Source identity Channel 0.1 installed Testing guide 0.1.6 candidate commit on Testing Testing 0.1 installed prior Stable guide 0.1.1 verified main commit tagged v0.1.1 Stable 0.1 historical Testing guide 0.1.2 unpublished Testing snapshot; not a Stable tag or operational bootstrap source Testing archive 0.1 historical Testing guide 0.1.3 unpublished Testing snapshot; not a Stable tag or artifact source Testing archive 0.1 failed-publication guide 0.1.4 immutable v0.1.4 tag and documentation only; no GitHub Release, signed plan, or release image Historical, non-installable 0.1 failed-publication guide 0.1.5 immutable v0.1.5 tag; candidate image digests built and signed, but no canonical plan, GitHub Release, or Stable tags Historical, non-installable 0.1 installed 0.1.6 Stable guide 0.1.6 exact verified main commit after it is tagged v0.1.6 and all signed/public artifacts pass Stable 0.1 public Stable guide 0.1.x current immutable release tag for the supported 0.1 line Stable

The shorter documentation label keeps patch-compatible guidance together. When a patch changes behavior or an operational procedure, the 0.1 Help Center is rebuilt from that accepted patch and its release notes describe the change. A future incompatible or feature release receives a new documentation line rather than rewriting 0.1 silently.

The channel is independent of SemVer. A Testing candidate and a Stable artifact may both report application version 0.1.6; only accepted main/tag provenance may claim a Stable application build. Public documentation can receive corrections on Testing, but a published Stable correction receives a new patch version and tag. The installed Help Center therefore remains authoritative for the exact binaries running in a deployment.

docs.title: Confirm what is installed
docs.text:
Use either of these sources:

  1. open the top-right release badge in the Console; or
  2. read /api/health/build-info from the same deployment.

Compare the reported application version and channel with the version context shown in the Help Center. If the Console and backend stamps disagree, the Console fails safe to Testing. Resolve that packaging mismatch before treating either component as a Stable release.

If a custom build contains uncommitted or local build metadata, use its bundled Help Center first and retain the deployment's own change record. Public documentation can describe only the closest accepted base release.

docs.title: Public Stable and Development material
docs.text:
The versioned public site complements the installed Help Center:

feature branches → Testing documentation review → main/tag Stable publication
  • Pull requests and Testing changes must pass a strict documentation build.
  • Testing output is a review artifact, not supported Stable guidance.
  • Promotion to main permits final verification; only the exact immutable release tag publishes the versioned Stable documentation and moves Stable aliases.
  • The stable and latest aliases point to the current supported documentation line after its release.
  • Previously published version directories remain available for older deployments.

The Stable publication maintains /0.1/; /stable/, /latest/, and the public-site root resolve to that supported line. A public version selector attempts to preserve the current page in the selected release line and falls back to that line's home page when the article did not exist.

Older public documentation displays an outdated-version warning. It remains useful for operating an older deployment, but later security or upgrade guidance may have superseded it. That warning concerns the selected public version; it does not make the documentation bundled with an older installed app inaccurate for that app.

docs.title: Repository publication prerequisites
docs.text:
Before a Stable documentation publish, repository administrators must:

  1. keep Testing and main as the integration and Stable branches, make main the default, and require the documented pull-request and CI gates;
  2. open Settings → Pages, set Build and deployment → Source to GitHub Actions, and protect the generated github-pages environment as appropriate for the repository;
  3. promote accepted documentation to main and verify that exact commit;
  4. create the matching immutable annotated release tag only after verification; and
  5. allow the Documentation workflow to complete its validate, publish, and deploy jobs for that tag.

The repository already uses main as its default branch and retains Testing as the integration branch. GitHub Actions Pages source selection is a one-time administrator setting; the workflow deliberately does not carry a personal access token that could change repository settings.

Pull requests, Testing pushes, and the promoted main commit validate and assemble review artifacts. Publication uses the exact annotated release tag after it is shown to match the verified main commit. The workflow then uses Mike to update generated history on gh-pages, assembles that history as a link-free Pages artifact, and deploys it with GitHub's native Pages actions. The gh-pages branch is generated version history, not the configured Pages publishing source. Untagged refs cannot move the public Stable site.

Generated public-site output is a release artifact. Do not edit it by hand; edit the Markdown on Testing, promote the accepted source through main, and let the documentation workflow republish it.

docs.title: Source and edit policy
docs.text:
The application-hosted Help Center is the reading surface. The repository is the authoring surface:

  • Stable documentation corresponds to accepted source on main and an immutable release tag.
  • Testing contains the next integrated documentation changes.
  • An edit proposed from an older rendered version must target the appropriate source history or intentionally update the current release line.

Do not replace an installed Help Center link with a raw repository link merely because both contain the same Markdown. The local rendered article is version-matched, searchable, themed, and available with the application; “View source” and “Edit this page” are secondary contributor actions.

See Agentic SOC 0.1, Release channels and versioning, and Upgrades.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: This list is part of the product contract for Agentic SOC 0.1.6 in Testing and, if the exact verified commit is published, its Stable artifacts. It distinguishes release gates from documented beta constraints so a green unit-test suite is never mistaken for release or production evidence.

docs.title: Repository protections require administrator verification
docs.text:
The canonical Testing and default main branches now exist, but branch protection, required checks, Pages source, and environment rules are GitHub repository settings; the application source cannot enforce or attest to them.

Required control: require the fail-closed CI passed aggregate and reviewed promotion into main, set Pages source to GitHub Actions, and protect the github-pages environment as appropriate. Verify those settings before treating a new commit or documentation deployment as accepted merely because its workflow ran.

docs.title: No project license
docs.text:
The repository does not contain a LICENSE file. Publicly visible source is not automatically open source and does not grant redistribution rights.

Required decision: choose and commit the intended license before publishing binaries, containers, or an “open-source” announcement. Apache-2.0 is permissive and patent-explicit; AGPL-3.0 requires network-service modifications to be offered to users. This is an owner/product decision and must not be guessed by automation.

docs.title: Signed update acceptance is external to local unit tests
docs.text:
The updater protocol, release plan, signature verification, rollback state machine, and reference Compose contracts have offline coverage. That does not prove the exact published v0.1.6 images and signed assets work through a real PostgreSQL Compose upgrade, interruption, cancellation, automatic rollback, and post-success rollback.

Required control: after the exact accepted main commit passes remote CI, publish the immutable tag artifacts, then run the documented isolated signed-update acceptance matrix against those public digests before enabling the Console update action for a supported deployment. Keep the action fail-closed until that evidence exists.

docs.title: Priority beta limitations
docs.text: The following constraints limit reproducibility, durability, topology, or stronger production claims. They remain explicit engineering priorities, but they are not all automatic blockers to publishing a clearly labelled beta release within its stated support boundary.

docs.title: Published release inputs are not fully reproducible
docs.text:
The immutable Stable-tag workflow now requires the annotated vX.Y.Z tag to resolve to the exact accepted main commit and pass the fail-closed CI aggregate. It builds multi-architecture backend, Web, and updater images once, publishes exact GHCR digests, emits SBOM/provenance attestations, signs every image and the declarative upgrade plan with the tag-bound GitHub Actions identity, and attaches the plan and Sigstore bundle to the GitHub Release.

Transitive Python resolution and container base images are not yet locked by reviewed hash/digest constraints. An attempt that fails before an exact draft contains its canonical plan can therefore resolve different upstream inputs when rerun. The draft is not public: the workflow stages both assets, downloads and byte-compares them, and verifies the signature before publishing it in one transition. A rerun may clean an interrupted starter upload or resume an exact tag/SHA draft, but never changes a published release. A complete plan pins the resulting application images exactly; a partial published asset set fails closed and requires a new patch release, and the plan does not prove its transitive inputs reproducible.

Required change: generate reviewed hash-locked Python constraints, pin every base image and tool action by immutable digest or commit with an update policy, record and compare a complete materials manifest, then prove reproducible rebuilds before making that stronger claim.

docs.title: Push receipt is not durable
docs.text:
Receivers currently normalise and process a batch in the backend process. Processing errors propagate so retry-capable transports can avoid acknowledging failed work, but there is no transactional receipt/inbox committed before correlation.

Consequences:

  • a process or host loss inside the receipt/processing window can lose an HTTP or lossy-syslog event;
  • there is no durable poison-event ledger or replay control;
  • queue acknowledgement behaviour must be certified per adapter;
  • receipt lag and oldest-unprocessed age cannot be measured centrally.

Required change: durable receipt + idempotency key + outbox, acknowledge only after receipt commit, retry workers, and a bounded dead-letter/replay workflow.

docs.title: Receiver checkpoints are not uniformly durable
docs.text:
Durable brokers retain acknowledged offsets, and the ES-compatible pull path now has a persisted cursor. Kinesis sequences and S3/GCS/Azure object markers now persist through the configured StateStore after successful processing. Local-file byte offsets and the default Event Hubs checkpoint path remain process-local. Restart can therefore replay or miss file data depending on start settings, while Event Hubs durability depends on wiring a supported checkpoint store.

Required change: persist per-source/partition/object/file checkpoints only after durable receipt, or require a native durable consumer/checkpoint store. Test crash and restart at every boundary, object overwrite/late arrival, file rotation, broker rebalance/reshard, and checkpoint corruption. Publish the actual guarantee per connector rather than one umbrella “durable” claim.

docs.title: Dynamic secrets do not survive restart
docs.text:
Per-source, notification, SSO, and locally registered model secrets entered through the UI/API live in process memory. Their configured field names may persist, but the values disappear when the backend restarts.

Required change: integrate a supported secret manager or encrypted secret store with rotation, versioning, audit, and explicit backup/restore semantics. Environment variables are a temporary boot-time path, not a complete multi-source lifecycle.

docs.title: No versioned database migrations
docs.text:
SQL state uses idempotent create_all and shared KV documents. There is no Alembic or equivalent ordered schema/data migration ledger, compatibility gate, or downgrade plan.

Required change: version every persisted schema and data transform; test clean install, forward upgrade, backup/restore, interrupted migration, and supported rollback for PostgreSQL. SQLite may remain a single-node evaluation profile.

docs.title: Open-case identity is too entity-centric
docs.text:
Configured sources now scope the active signature by source, so the same entity from source A and source B creates distinct cases that the related-case/campaign layer can link. Within one source, however, identity is still essentially (source_id, entity_type, entity_value). While a case remains open, a later and potentially unrelated rule family or distant episode on the same user, host, or address can attach to it. The legacy unconfigured path remains entity-only. This can over-merge distinct stories and distort evidence, risk, ownership, and timing.

Required change: version the case-signature policy and add a bounded incident episode or strong native lineage within each source. Keep deterministic event/detection idempotency separate from the decision to attach, relate, or open a new case. Add tests for retries of one incident, distinct rules on the same entity, NAT/shared IPs, distant/reopened activity, legacy migration, and cross-source related-but-not-merged cases.

docs.title: One-click updates support one deployment profile
docs.text:
The unpublished 0.1.2 snapshot introduced source discovery and coherent-pair activation but did not publish the host supervisor or signed upgrade plan. Version 0.1.6 carries the version-1 supervisor protocol and canonical base-Compose contract without broadening its supported topology. It still cannot retroactively install a privileged host component. A supported canonical v0.1.1 installation requires one manual scripts/bootstrap-updater.sh step from the clean, exact annotated v0.1.6 tag whose commit remains contained in origin/main; that step delegates the full v0.1.1→v0.1.6 transition to the signed plan. Testing/source-built 0.1.3 and the non-installable v0.1.4/v0.1.5 attempts must instead be reconciled manually and cannot be relabelled Stable. Subsequent compatible Stable releases can be installed from the Console only for the reference, single-replica standalone Docker Compose topology with PostgreSQL-owned state, durable authentication/secrets, a coherent known build/schema identity, a base Compose file matching the signed canonical SHA-256, canonical project/network/service and PostgreSQL-volume identity, and a signed plan whose migration strategy is none.

The updater never transports or replaces the base Compose file. The 0.1.x protocol pins its version-invariant bytes in deploy/update-base-v1.sha256, while signed release overrides carry component versions and digests. Sequential patch upgrades therefore retain one base; changing it requires a new protocol and manual bootstrap.

PostgreSQL and Redis infrastructure images are deliberately unchanged. SQLite, Elasticsearch-owned state, external PostgreSQL, the legacy ELK composition, custom/forked Compose layouts, Kubernetes, horizontal replicas, runtime-only UI secrets, migration-bearing releases, and incompatible updater protocols are blocked with a manual remediation. Automatic rollback depends on retained prior application image IDs and never restores PostgreSQL. The verified quiesced dump is a break-glass artifact for explicit operator recovery; a host or storage failure that destroys those recovery assets remains a manual disaster-recovery event. Image rollback cannot undo an incompatible data change, which is why migration-bearing plans fail preflight. Supervisor self-replacement uses a restartable helper whose name-swap transaction is idempotent across ordinary helper-process, Docker-daemon, and host restarts. A failure that prevents Docker and all of its containers from running, or destroys Docker metadata/storage, remains an operator-owned host recovery event. After bootstrap, raw Compose invocations are unsupported; use scripts/agentic-soc-compose.sh so the active digest override remains in force and mutating lifecycle commands serialize with the supervised updater. The guard cannot protect an operator who deliberately bypasses it with raw Docker or Compose commands. An unknown, malformed, or orphaned durable update marker intentionally fails closed and requires operator reconciliation; only an exact terminal ledger job is cleared automatically after restart.

The supervisor has Docker-socket authority, which is effectively root-equivalent on the host, and is therefore part of the trusted computing base rather than an ordinary application sidecar. Official update plans are also anonymously pull-only: the three GHCR packages must be public because the supervisor intentionally stores no registry credential. See Upgrades.

docs.title: Updater artifacts are not auto-pruned
docs.text:
The updater foundation included in version 0.1.6 retains updater jobs, preflights, signed plan assets, receipts, and deployment snapshots in the updater-state volume and verified PostgreSQL dumps in the updater-backup volume. It does not implement age-, count-, or status-based pruning. Operators must monitor capacity for both volumes and retain, at minimum, every active job, the latest terminal record, the current installed release's rollback evidence, any terminal outcome not yet mirrored into application audit, and every break-glass artifact still covered by local policy.

History is eligible for operator-controlled archive or removal only after a later successful release supersedes its rollback authority, its exact terminal transition is confirmed in append-only application audit, and backup/retention policy permits. There is no supported live per-record purge in this release. Automatic cleanup needs a future updater/backend protocol that acknowledges the audit mirror, identifies the authoritative rollback generation, carries policy holds, and commits crash-safe retention decisions; the updater cannot safely infer those facts from timestamps or a terminal status alone.

docs.title: Single replica only
docs.text:
Run exactly one backend replica. Signature locks, receiver ownership, schedulers, recent-event buffers, and the realtime event bus are process-local. The storage abstractions do not yet provide all of the leases, uniqueness constraints, and atomic claims needed for active-active replicas.

Adding replicas now can duplicate cases or scheduled work, lose receiver ownership, and deliver inconsistent live updates. The scale-out roadmap defines the required worker/lease split.

docs.title: Volatile push evidence and realtime replay
docs.text:
Push-source browse/live-tail keeps only the latest 500 events per source in process memory. Realtime SSE replay is also process-local. Restarting the backend clears both, and another replica would not share them.

Cases retain selected event IDs and evidence, but the suite does not yet provide a durable raw-event archive for pushed data. Keep the authoritative event in the source/broker/object store during evaluation.

docs.title: Receiver supervision is process-local
docs.text: Source create/update/delete and secret rotation now reconcile the live receiver set with a coarse stop-and-rebuild cycle. A failed long-running receiver is restarted with bounded exponential backoff, preserving broker redelivery after processing errors. There is still no persisted last-error/restart state, lease, or distributed ownership, and a permanently invalid configuration retries locally until corrected. Verify the health/coverage surface after topology changes and alert on repeated receiver restart logs during evaluation.

docs.title: Pull replay and late-arrival handling are bounded
docs.text:
